title: Decide how app-target logic gets tested at all
acceptance: A decision on where tests for app-target code live: an iOS unit test target, a second local SPM package for pure app logic, or an accepted permanent gap
If a test target: the cost to the gate is measured, since an iOS test target needs a booted simulator and D-0001 chose SPM precisely to avoid that
ReaderContrastAudit is wired into whatever is chosen, so the palette cannot regress silently
notes: DECIDED 2026-08-25 under delegated authority: a SECOND local SPM package for pure app logic, not an iOS unit test target. Rationale: D-0001 chose SPM to keep the gate simulator-free, and it works — the whole gate runs in ~20s with no simctl contention, which is what lets worktrees verify in parallel. An iOS test target would claw that back for the whole suite in order to test a handful of pure functions. The logic that actually needs coverage is pure: contrast ratio math over hex values, and search snippet extraction over strings. Neither needs SwiftUI, SwiftData, or a device. What stays in the app target is what genuinely depends on the frameworks — SwiftData predicates, view bodies, Color wrappers. EVIDENCE, not speculation: two casualties in one session. ReaderContrastAudit (T-0014) landed as 160 lines of dead code because nothing could call it, and T-0015 fixed a ranking bug that /code-review caught, then could not add a committed regression test for it. Both would have been ordinary unit tests in a package.
